races.name: Title Sponsor Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Kisiyra
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has finished 3rd-5th repeatedly at this sort of trip; Good-ground form is workable (4/9 sim-going) but the tongue-tie is notable and she has never won on Good; David Thompson yard is quiet over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: This mare failed to see out an even longer trip when well beaten at Hamilton last time, but today's shorter test sits closer to her ideal range of 8 to 11 furlongs. She's had her share of issues and is without a win in her last four starts, so proof of ability is needed before she can be trusted, with a rating of 66 reflecting a modest look on paper.

runners_data.name: Izzari
runners_data.note: In-form trainer Iain Jardine (8/28 T14) is a strong angle, but Izzari's last six runs show finishes of 6-4-8-0-0 and she has only one win in 15 similar-going starts; prominent style suits the race shape but raw form is modest.
runners_data.comment: This gelding's rating of 79 puts him third best of this field on pure figures, making him hard to ignore if he can rediscover his level. He's been below par of late, down the field in a handicap at York most recently, with his official mark easing as a result; he stays 11 furlongs but could even be better suited by a shorter trip.

runners_data.name: Eagles Dream
runners_data.note: 316 days off the track is the headline concern; however, she ran 3-3-4 in her last three starts on Good ground and handles this trip well — if Tristan Davidson has her ready, the hold-up style sits in a minority here and a clean run could make her dangerous.
runners_data.comment: A filly who has been off the track for the best part of a year, she ran to her level when beaten three lengths off a 3lb higher mark at Killarney in August, her sole start since, and manifestly needs the run following such a lengthy absence. Effective from 10 to 12 furlongs and rated only 67, she's up against it fresh on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with solid placed form (0W2P on similar going), including a 2nd last time out on Soft; Josephine Gordon is a strong booking and the 6-year-old stays further than this, suggesting 9f on Good could be on the sharp side.
runners_data.comment: Back in form across both codes recently, this gelding ranks second on our figures at a rating of 82 and remains a serious threat. The query is more about conditions than ability: he already seemed to want a tougher test when beaten 2 1/4 lengths off a 1lb lower mark at Ayr last time, and today's shorter trip, well inside his best of two miles, could be on the sharp side for him.

runners_data.name: Krissy
runners_data.note: The race's confirmed front-runner with a strong recent record (4W in 9 similar-going starts, 211061 form), though the STYLE_FIT tag signals she may be racing slightly out of preferred role here; Jim Goldie sends her back quickly (12 days) and the flat Carlisle track suits a front-runner who can control tempo.
runners_data.comment: This mare boasts three wins in her last six starts, including a half-length success at Musselburgh last time when allowed an uncontested lead off a 3lb lower mark. She needs to dictate from the front to be seen at her best, which could be the deciding factor from stall three, but on form figures alone she's a leading threat at a rating of 78.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby runner (15/81 T14 — yard in form) but Financer's own figures are modest with no wins in 12 similar-ground runs and a blinker fitted; hold-up style means she needs things to go right in running and the pace here may not be strong enough to suit.
runners_data.comment: A picture of consistency without a win in his last five starts, this gelding ran to par when beaten three lengths off a 1lb higher mark here last time, and he races for a yard with an excellent record at the course. First-time blinkers may sharpen him up further, and with this trip suiting, he's rated 73 and worth another chance.

runners_data.name: Hostility
runners_data.note: Sharp recent form — 1st and 2nd in last two starts, both on Good ground over 7f-9f — and David O'Meara's yard is firing (7/47 T14); stepping up to 9f for the first time in a while is the one question, but a prominent style in a race shaped for that profile makes her live.
runners_data.comment: In excellent form, this gelding made smooth headway from off the pace to win with a little in hand here last time, doing so from a mark 3lb lower than he carries today. Versatile on ground and effective from 6 to 9 furlongs, he's rated 83, right at the head of this field on figures, with the only query being whether he repeats that same finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Bellasio
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's consistent handicapper has placed three times in 14 similar-going runs; naturally wants to race prominently but with traffic ahead of her in this field she is likely to be shuffled wider back than suits, which tempers her chance despite the respectable placed record.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last five starts but continuing to build towards his peak, this gelding was beaten only half a length off a 1lb lower mark here last time, with his current mark now more workable for him. He can be fractious beforehand, but with the yard in form and conditions to suit at 8 to 9 furlongs, he's rated 71 and capable of featuring.

runners_data.name: Jewel Maker
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old who has only one win in 15 similar-going starts and whose recent form reads 9-0-7-4-8; front-running tendency will be compromised by the number of prominent rivals, and age-related decline makes finding a winning effort a tall order here.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten when dropped to a mile in a handicap here last time, this gelding remains without a win in his last five starts and sits bottom of these figures on a rating of 64. His only worthwhile effort recently came in a race for apprentice riders, and he needs plenty to turn around at this level even with today's trip back in his 8-10f range.

races.paceDynamic: Krissy is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to push her hard from the outset, she should be able to dictate at a sensible, sustainable gallop over this 1m1f trip on Good ground at Carlisle. Kisiyra, Izzari, and Hostility all sit in the prominent bracket and will track Krissy through the early stages, meaning there is a cluster of horses hunting the same piece of ground rather than pressing the pace aggressively. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their favoured positions — Bellasio and Jewel Maker are natural prominent racers who are highly likely to find themselves racing further back than ideal, unable to dominate the position they prefer. The resulting shape — a controlled, honest pace set by a single front-runner with a pack pressing just behind — is most likely to favour horses who can travel prominently within themselves and produce a sustained finish rather than a single sharp sprint, rewarding those with proven Good-ground form at this sort of trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Krissy Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy leads at a comfortable gallop and the prominent trackers travel smoothly in her slipstream.
scenarios.body: Krissy sets an unhurried but genuine tempo and the closers never get into a rhythm to reel her in; horses like Kisiyra and Hostility, grinding in her wake, are best positioned to pounce if she fades late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Runs On
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy's early lead is softened by a prominent challenger pressing her harder than expected, burning her out.
scenarios.body: A contested pace damages the front-runner and opens the door for a prominent tracker sitting just off the pace to sprint through; Hostility's recent 1-2 form on Good ground makes her a prime beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely strong enough early to string the field out and leave hold-up horses with ground to make.
scenarios.body: Mr Lincoln and Eagles Dream, natural hold-up types with credible Good-ground form, get a clean run through the pack in the straight; Eagles Dream's recent 3-3 placings on Good ground give her claims if the pace truly suits a late charge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Bellasio or Jewel Maker, pushed wider back than ideal, manage to produce a late forward move from midfield.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires both horses to race significantly out of role and still travel well enough to overhaul those in front — unlikely given their style mismatch and Jewel Maker's age and recent modest form.

watchPoints.text: Hostility (Joanna Mason) has finished 1st and 2nd in her last two starts on Good ground and her prominent style puts her exactly where the race shape rewards — watch for her tracking Krissy through the bend.
Krissy is the sole confirmed front-runner and if she gets a clear, uncontested lead from flag to the turn, her recent winning form (four wins in nine Good-ground starts) makes her very hard to catch.

Eagles Dream returns from 316 days off; if Tristan Davidson has freshened her for this spot, her Good-ground placed form (3-3-4) and hold-up style could make her a well-priced runner if the early pace is honest enough.

Bellasio and Jewel Maker are both natural prominent types who will likely be shuffled back — watch whether either can find a clear outside route in the straight, as their true pace preference will push them forward regardless of position.

Iain Jardine's double-runner angle (Izzari and Mr Lincoln, T14 8/28) is worth noting — the yard is in a strong spell and one of the two may be the better-fancied stable runner, worth monitoring market moves before the off.

races.name: Style Awards Fashion Finale Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Wrist Art
runners_data.note: Has placed twice on Good ground at today's trip and beyond in recent history (4th at 10f, 3rd at 10f), and is a genuine hold-up type whose best chance depends on the pace being true; tongue tie fitted, 5 days since last run and appears to have reasonable fitness.
runners_data.comment: Faded from the front rank to finish fourth, beaten eight lengths, unable to last home over a testing mile and a quarter at Pontefract last time. A drop back to today's sharper trip, alongside the addition of a tongue-tie and visor, could bring a much-needed leap forward, and he's without a win in his last six starts but rates a solid fourth on our figures at 52.

runners_data.name: Misemerald
runners_data.note: Recent form shows back-to-back placed efforts at 7-9f, but her last five runs include no Good-ground wins and she is a true hold-up horse whose chances are tempered by being unable to settle where she needs to given the volume of similar types in this field.
runners_data.comment: Performed to expectation when runner-up, beaten a length and a half off a marginally lower mark at Catterick last time, dropped in trip to 7f that day. Stepping back up to today's mile suits her proven range, and on a fair weight she sits mid-field on our figures at 51, still without a win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Captain Pickles
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, and an OR=55 horse with recent wins on Synthetic surface; the big question is whether Good turf over 1m suits after only two similar-going runs, but no rival is likely to push them off the front.
runners_data.comment: A below-par third, beaten seven lengths in a handicap at Wolverhampton, was the exception in an otherwise consistent campaign that had brought three wins from his previous five starts. Fifty-four days off since, but proven over today's trip and going, he's only mid-pack on our figures at 49 pending a return closer to his best.

runners_data.name: Book Of Life
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with five placed efforts in the last six starts, handles a range of distances around today's trip, and from the chair of Joanna Mason is likely to be produced smoothly to chase Captain Pickles — limited Similar-going form is a caveat.
runners_data.comment: Twice a runner-up among his last six starts and still without a win, he found turf tougher going when beaten seven lengths in a handicap at Hamilton last time, a below-par run after some good form on the all-weather. First-time cheekpieces are added as he continues to search for that first solid effort on grass, and he rates second in our figures on 63 despite the query over the surface.

runners_data.name: Mertoun
runners_data.note: The standout form horse on good ground with a recent win at 8f and a placed effort at the same trip on Good, trained by Jane Chapple-Hyam whose yard is in form (5/13 over 14 days); a 3-year-old dropping into a Pro-Am contest is a significant class edge.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap by five and a half lengths at Windsor last time when pushed out, doing so with perhaps a bit more in hand than the bare result suggests off a mark ten pounds lower than today's. With the yard in good form and effective at today's trip and ground, he tops our figures on 65 and rates the one to beat, even up in the weights after that success.

runners_data.name: Top Gun Tina
runners_data.note: All five recent runs came on Standard (Synthetic) turf so there is a real unknown about whether Good ground suits; a natural hold-up horse who is unlikely to find the rear rail given the congestion of closers, which blunts her effectiveness here.
runners_data.comment: A model of consistency at this level, she matched that level when fourth, beaten three and a quarter lengths off a marginally higher mark at Newcastle last time. Well suited by today's trip, but she is having her first run in 75 days, and rates third in our figures on 58 among the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Wheres The Crumpet
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old whose last five starts all came on Synthetic or Good and produced only placing at best, and though a true hold-up type she has been unable to get that position given the field make-up — recent form figures include a 0 (fell/unseated) so reliability is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Question marks over stamina were raised when well beaten down the field over 10f in a classified event at Newcastle last time, extending a spell out of sorts without a win in her last six starts. First-time cheekpieces and a return to a sharper trip on today's ground, which she has raced over before, offer some hope of a bounce, but she's only seventh on our figures at 43.

runners_data.name: Shoptilyoudrop
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old who has raced mainly at 6-7f on Synthetic and Soft, making today's Good-ground mile a potential double query on both surface and distance; genuinely inclined to come from off the pace but the race shape makes that difficult.
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten fifth when dropped to 6f in a handicap at Hamilton last time continued a run without a win in her last five starts, with her only form of real note coming on synthetic ground. Up in trip again today, beyond the 7f she seems to prefer, she sits towards the bottom of our figures on 40 and has plenty to find before she can feature.

runners_data.name: Sanny Doo
runners_data.note: A lightly-weighted 3-year-old from Jim Goldie's yard (3 winners from 38 runners in 14 days) whose form figures include three 8s in recent starts — a hold-up horse unable to get to the back naturally, and the Good-ground mile represents a step up in both trip and quality.
runners_data.comment: Never able to threaten before being eased down well beaten in a handicap at Musselburgh last time, he's shown little to suggest a change in fortunes across his last five starts. First-time cheekpieces are the obvious card to play, but he anchors our figures at 39 and has plenty to find on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Can I Kiss You
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — ignore for race analysis purposes; the horse does not take part.

races.paceDynamic: Captain Pickles is the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no genuine rival willing or able to press them from the outset, should control the pace from the gates on Carlisle's flat mile without serious pressure. The tempo will likely be honest but manageable — a solo leader setting their own rhythm on Good turf creates a classic leader-friendly shape where energy is conserved through the middle sections before a controlled kick entering the straight. Mertoun, Wrist Art and Book Of Life are the runners best positioned to take advantage from just off the pace, while Misemerald, Top Gun Tina, Wheres The Crumpet, Shoptilyoudrop and Sanny Doo are all genuine hold-up types who cannot all settle at the rear as their style demands — the field holds more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate, and those most likely to secure something close to their natural position are Mertoun and Wrist Art, given their proven ability at this trip on Good ground. This race shape overwhelmingly favours front-running or prominently-ridden types who can control the pace, with hold-up horses disadvantaged by the likely lack of a true searching gallop and by being forced out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Captain Pickles Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Pickles leads from the front without any rival willing to harry them, setting a steady-to-fair gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Captain Pickles controls every yard of the race, ensuring the pace is never truly searching, which makes it extremely difficult for genuine closers to generate the momentum needed to reel them in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse settled in second or third in the slipstream of Captain Pickles produces a sharper turn of foot at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Mertoun, who has the best recent form in the field including a win on Good ground and a runner-up at 8f on the same surface, is perfectly placed to execute this move, as is Book Of Life who has consistent placed form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Pickles sets a surprisingly fast early tempo and the pace proves unsustainable, leaving the door ajar for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Wrist Art, with placed form on Good ground and enough tactical versatility, is best equipped among the closers to capitalise, though most genuine hold-up types are pushed out of their natural position by the congested rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Pace, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses attempt to assert early position despite their natural hold-up styles, creating interference and an uneven gallop.
scenarios.body: A bunched mid-race scenario could create a lottery in the final furlong, with Mertoun's class and recent winning form giving a marginal edge in a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Captain Pickles is unopposed at the front — if they are allowed to bowl along at their own tempo for the full mile, their rivals may simply run out of time to close, making them a central danger regardless of handicap mark.

Mertoun's class stands out on recent form figures (1W2P in last 5 on Good) but as a 3-year-old carrying 147lbs in a Pro-Am contest, the jockey factor (Alexandra Egan) could be decisive — watch whether they can hold a position close to Captain Pickles throughout.

The sheer number of hold-up types — Misemerald, Top Gun Tina, Wheres The Crumpet, Shoptilyoudrop and Sanny Doo — all competing for the rear means the final furlongs could see multiple horses switching wide simultaneously; any runner caught in traffic at the two-furlong mark will likely be out of the reckoning.

Book Of Life's jockey Joanna Mason is one of the most experienced riders in this Pro-Am field — her ability to place a horse smoothly behind a sole leader and time a challenge on the descent to the finish at Carlisle is worth factoring into positioning assessments.

Top Gun Tina and Shoptilyoudrop (both trained by David Thompson, T14:0/7) have shown no recent winners from the yard — a form concern worth noting when assessing their likelihood of improving on current handicap marks today.

races.name: Sheila Petch Appreciation Handicap (For Professional Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Bravo Zulu
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has shown she can produce a sharp finish over shorter trips, but her best form sits at 6-7f and this mile on Good turf at Carlisle is at the outer edge of her comfortable range; 15 days since last run is fine and Laura Pearson rides.
runners_data.comment: In and out of form across six starts, this gelding was about right when beaten 2 1/4 lengths off a higher mark at Newmarket last time. He's proven at today's trip and ground, and a first-time eyeshield may add consistency, but needs more to feature prominently.

runners_data.name: Inspired
runners_data.note: Taryn Langley (5lb claimer) takes the ride and the four-year-old has solid recent form placing over 7-8f on Goodwood Soft and Stansted, but the prominent style suits this scenario well and her sim-going record here (3 finishes from 8) hints at a degree of going familiarity.
runners_data.comment: Consistent with three places in his recent starts, this gelding was about right when beaten 2 1/4 lengths off a higher mark at York last time. He's proven over today's trip and ground and ranks second of seven on our figures, but is yet to turn the form into a win.

runners_data.name: Calyxoh
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front runner in this field, giving her complete control of the tempo; her headline form figures look modest but her best effort was a second from the front and her sim-going record shows she handles Good turf, while Alexandra Egan (7lb claimer) takes a useful allowance.
runners_data.comment: An indifferent spell continues, following a below-form run in Dubai with an eighth-length defeat in a Chester handicap last time. He does have today's trip and ground covered, though, and first-time cheekpieces offer hope for the outsider of this field.

runners_data.name: Jannas Journey
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's five-year-old has a prominent style that suits sitting just off the leader, but her last five runs all came over 8f at Carlisle on Good, producing only placed results at best, and Lauren Young's 5lb claim keeps the weight manageable at 133lbs.
runners_data.comment: Ranked third of seven on our figures and clear of her official mark, with form over today's trip and ground. She can carry her head high under pressure and was a shade below form at York last time, but on a sounder round she's the danger here.

runners_data.name: Benacre
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's six-year-old carries strong placed form over 7f on Good turf and Joanna Mason is a significant booking, but this horse's natural inclination is to race prominently — with Calyxoh already filling that role, Benacre will likely have to settle in midfield against her instincts, which tempers her winning prospects in this shape.
runners_data.comment: An improved effort when beaten 7 lengths in a Newmarket handicap last time suggests this gelding is finding form again, having slipped below the mark that once brought success. He's effective at today's trip and ground, ranks fourth of seven on our figures, but still has a bit to prove.

runners_data.name: The Green Man
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's seven-year-old is a genuine front-runner in most races, with consistent placed efforts over 7f on Soft and Standard; squeezed back into a midfield slot in this shape by Calyxoh's presence, Josephine Gordon will need a tactical change to unlock his best, and his Carlisle form on Good is limited (2 from 15 sim-going).
runners_data.comment: Consistently in the frame with three thirds and a second from six runs, this gelding ran close to form when beaten 2 lengths off a higher mark at Doncaster last time. He's proven at today's trip and tries a first-time tongue-tie and visor, though he's near bottom on our figures.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up type has a strong record of placing over 8f on Good turf — five placed efforts in her last five starts at that trip — and Faye McManoman rides; she is the most naturally suited hold-up horse in this field, needing either a contested pace or a late sprint scenario to get competitive.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated on our figures, this gelding confirmed his consistency when beaten 2 1/4 lengths off a lower mark at this course last time. From a yard with a fine record here and sporting first-time cheekpieces, he's the one to beat, though he must finally turn those places into a win.

races.paceDynamic: Calyxoh is the confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine rival willing to take her on for the lead, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this mile at Carlisle. Inspired and Jannas Journey are the most likely to press her in the early stages from a prominent position, though neither is a natural front-runner, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. This setup — a single unchallenged leader over a flat mile on Good turf — strongly favours horses that can travel prominently and produce a turn of foot in the straight, rather than those relying on a pace collapse to close from the rear. The field holds more prominent-profile types than can all secure their natural position: Benacre and The Green Man are both genuine front-runners in typical races but have been displaced to midfield in this shape, meaning Calyxoh and Inspired are best-placed to fill the early slots ahead of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Calyxoh Controls, Prominent Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Calyxoh leads at a comfortable clip and the race is run at an honest but not pressured pace, allowing the closest pursuers to time their challenge.
scenarios.body: Calyxoh sets a metronomic gallop and the race becomes a test of who can sustain that rhythm longest, with prominent horses having the advantage of tracking the leader without burning extra energy weaving through traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Calyxoh sets an unusually slow tempo that bunches the field and creates a sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A truly muddling gallop compresses the field so tightly that hold-up horses find room to produce their finish, with Barley's consistent placed form over this course and distance putting her in the frame.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Scrap, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Benacre or The Green Man push forward to contest the lead, injecting more pace and turning this into a stronger-run race than Calyxoh wants.
scenarios.body: A genuine contested gallop stretches the field and drains the leaders, opening the door for hold-up horses who have more left in the tank entering the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Leader Wins Easily
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so sedate and unchallenged that Calyxoh simply coasts home without any rival getting into contention.
scenarios.body: A total procession unfolds as no rival has the speed to close on a fresh, well-placed leader given no ammunition by the gallop, and those racing prominently behind her can only fill the minor placings.

watchPoints.text: Calyxoh's early establishment of the lead is the hinge point of the race — if she is pressured by Benacre or The Green Man jumping out boldly, the whole tempo dynamic changes and her chance is significantly compromised.

Benacre and The Green Man may both instinctively try to stride forward from the gates, creating an unplanned speed duel in the first two furlongs that transforms this from a dawdle into a genuine test; watch market moves on both.

Barley's hold-up profile is dependent on at least a fair pace — if the race is run at a canter and she is last or second-last turning in, she may simply have too much ground to make up in the straight at Carlisle.

Taryn Langley (5) on Inspired and Lauren Young (5) on Jannas Journey mean 10lbs of claim between two prominent horses — if either jockey positions too aggressively early chasing Calyxoh, they risk burning their mount's finishing effort.

Bravo Zulu's most productive form sits at 6-7f; the step up to 1m is a recurring question mark and any strong pace scenario will suit her more than a pedestrian one where the lack of a true test at this trip becomes an issue.

races.name: Helen Stewart Appreciation Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Junkyard Dog
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has shown sim-going form (6/15) and wears headgear (v); 25 days since last run is fine, but a field of five with one front-runner may not generate enough late pace collapse to suit a horse arriving from so far back — Cara Tuke claiming 5lbs softens the weight imposition but tactical improvement is needed.
runners_data.comment: Well held in a handicap last time after switching back from hurdling, this gelding remains without a win having managed no better than 9th, 8th, 5th, 4th and 5th in recent starts. A first-time visor and a yard in good form offer a glimmer of hope, but rated only 57 off a mark of 67, there's plenty for him to find.

runners_data.name: Alpine Sierra
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has won this trip and trip-adjacent races on good ground multiple times — three wins from recent good-ground starts underlines her strong going/distance profile; as the sole front-runner she has a clear positional advantage, though her STYLE_FIT tag is a reminder she is racing at the top of her natural envelope and must not be given undue credit beyond what the shape alone already gives her.
runners_data.comment: This gelding ran up a hat-trick before that sequence ended, and a return to that level would make him hard to hold out, especially as he won here previously off a lower mark than his current 148 lb, and he's drawn in stall four this time. Rated 71, the obvious threat to that is a repeat of the notably faster ground that undid him last time, conditions that look on the cards again today.

runners_data.name: Valley Of Flowers
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with three placed efforts at the highest-frequency position in similar going; Joanna Mason is a strong booking and the 12-day turnaround is sharp — her 0W record in sim-going mitigates optimism, but consistent placed form (3 of 5 recent) over this sort of trip makes her a key late interest in a race where closers are competing for limited real estate.
runners_data.comment: A picture of consistency without a win in her last five starts, this mare confirmed she retains her form when only beaten 3 1/4 lengths off a 1lb higher mark at Catterick last time, and she's proven over today's trip and ground. Top-rated at 78, she looks the one to be positive about, with any doubt centred on her attitude under pressure.

runners_data.name: Covert Legend
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose true style means the midfield slot shown on the map is not where she will naturally settle — headgear (t, tongue-tie) noted, and 8 days since last run is quick; her zero wins and zero places in sim-going across 15 starts is a concerning data point, and the STYLE_FIT tag compounds the concern that she cannot recapture her best tactical position in this compressed field.
runners_data.comment: A model of consistency who was only beaten two lengths at the Curragh last time, this gelding steps up today with a first-time tongue-tie that could sharpen him further. He's yet to convert that form into a win in his last five starts, but effective from 9 to 12 furlongs on a sound surface and rated 72, he's clearly one of this race's leading dangers.

runners_data.name: V Twelve
runners_data.note: True hold-up type mapped to midfield as the field cannot accommodate all hold-up runners at the rear — 87 days since last run (56J) is a significant fitness flag; Josephine Gordon is the key positive, a jockey with the tactical intelligence to maximise a hold-up horse's chance, but V Twelve's interrupted preparation and a single win in 15 sim-going starts tempers expectations substantially.
runners_data.comment: This gelding has posted a win and two thirds among his last five starts, form that keeps him firmly in the mix at a rating of 60 from stall three under 144 lb. The obvious concern is finding that level again, having been well beaten after a switch to fences most recently, following a moderate effort on the level before that.

races.paceDynamic: Alpine Sierra is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no credible challenger for the lead, will bowl along at a controlled, self-set tempo over 1m3f on good ground at Carlisle. That unchallenged rhythm is likely to be genuinely sustainable rather than reckless, giving Alpine Sierra every chance to steal a march on rivals who will be forced to make ground from behind. The three hold-up horses — Junkyard Dog, Valley Of Flowers, and the redistributed pair Covert Legend and V Twelve — will all be hunting the same closing ground late, creating congestion at the rear end of the field. This shape strongly favours a horse that can race prominently or produce a well-timed mid-race move to bridge the gap, rather than a deep closer relying on a true pace collapse that may never come. The field holds more genuine hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Alpine Sierra is virtually certain to lead, while Covert Legend and V Twelve, natural hold-up types, are shown in midfield positions they are unlikely to naturally occupy in this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alpine Sierra Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Alpine Sierra goes unchallenged to the front and controls tempo throughout, denying closers a meaningful target to aim at.
scenarios.body: Alpine Sierra sets a measured gallop on good ground over a trip she has already proven she relishes, and with no one willing or able to press her she reaches the home turn with a decisive advantage in hand. Horses with a prominent or patient mid-race profile who can make smooth headway — rather than deep closers hunting a collapse — are best placed to chase her down.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Alpine Sierra's solo lead becomes overly generous and she ties up in the final furlong, opening the race for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: An uncontested front-runner occasionally misjudges her own pace and fades sharply inside the final two furlongs, handing late-movers a sprint to the line. Junkyard Dog and Valley Of Flowers, who are genuine hold-up types with similar-going form, are best positioned to benefit from that late surge — though this outcome hinges on a tempo error that good ground makes less likely.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Move Decisive
scenarios.trigger: If one of the midfield-mapped horses presses forward during the race to bridge the gap and strikes on the home turn.
scenarios.body: Covert Legend or V Twelve, both natural hold-up runners pushed to a midfield map position in this race shape, would need to race out of character and sustain a long run from off the pace to make this scenario work. The style-fit penalties on both horses reduce confidence, but the compacted field means even a modest, timely forward move could prove decisive on good ground at a track that does favour those who travel smoothly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Total Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so modest that the whole field converges in the straight and the outcome is decided by fine margins.
scenarios.body: With five runners and one sole pace-setter, an unusually slow gallop could compress the field into a bunch sprint over the final two furlongs, nullifying positional advantage entirely. This scenario remains unlikely given Alpine Sierra's strong front-running record and the trip, but Josephine Gordon on V Twelve has the craft to exploit it if it materialises.

watchPoints.text: Alpine Sierra's early stride pattern — if Lauren Young eases her into a crawl rather than a controlled rhythm, the entire field could sweep past her in the straight; conversely, if she skips clear by two lengths at the half-mile, the closers face an enormous task on good ground.

Junkyard Dog's wide draw and hold-up style means Cara Tuke will need to find ground quickly once the field rounds into the straight — watch for her being blocked by the three midfield/hold-up horses who will all be tracking the same ground simultaneously.

V Twelve's 87-day absence (56 days jockey-out) is the race's biggest fitness unknown — Martin Todhunter's 1/3 strike rate over 14 days suggests the yard is quiet, and a horse returning from a break of this length over 1m3f on good ground needs to show early evidence of well-being or may simply be outpaced.

Valley Of Flowers has the most consistent placed record of the hold-up trio in this going, but Samantha & Jacqueline Coward's trainer 14-day figure of 0/3 is worth noting — if the yard is out of form, her market position may flatter her chance slightly.

With all five runners carrying 144–149lbs and the race run as a pro-am female jockey handicap, jockey-weight differentials are compressed — Cara Tuke's 5lb claim on Junkyard Dog is the only meaningful weight relief in the race and could matter in a tight finish.

races.name: Caledonia Park Stylish Stayers Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Laravie
runners_data.note: Has won four of her last five starts including three consecutive victories over distances of 14f-17f on good ground, making her the clear form pick; the visor is retained and Joanna Mason has a strong record here, though any STYLE_FIT discount applies if she is somehow squeezed off a dominating lead.
runners_data.comment: Progressive with a hat-trick of wins before a good second last time under a 3lb rise, this mare is the one to beat on our figures. She's proven over today's trip and ground, tries a first-time visor, though her modest speed figure is the one query.

runners_data.name: Tarbat Ness
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent racer whose recent form (4-4-5-6-4) over 16f on similar ground shows consistent placing without winning, and trainer John Berry's 0 from 5 in the last 14 days is not encouraging; likely to fill the chasing role behind Laravie without threatening.
runners_data.comment: Generally in good form, with a third beaten 5 1/4 lengths in a Kempton handicap last time, this gelding is clearly suited by this longer trip. He ranks second of six on our figures and tries first-time blinkers, though his modest speed figure is the one query.

runners_data.name: Cascade Hall
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who has won twice from six recent starts on good ground and hit the frame four more times, with Lauren Young taking the ride for a Jim Goldie yard that has been running well (3/38 in 14 days); the step up to 2m1f on good turf looks well-suited to her profile.
runners_data.comment: A dual winner this term, including a 6 1/2-length success off a lower mark two starts back, this gelding backed that up with a creditable third last time. He's proven on this ground and ranks third of six on our figures, but today's trip may stretch him beyond his best 12-16f range.

runners_data.name: Rupert The Prince
runners_data.note: Naturally wants to race prominently but with Laravie and Tarbat Ness ahead of him in the queue, he is likely to find himself further back than ideal; his best recent effort was 2nd over 21f on good ground, so the trip is fine, but the style mismatch tempers expectations significantly.
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten effort for no obvious reason in a Pontefract handicap last time was a big letdown after a promising campaign that included a win and a narrow second. He's proven at today's trip and ground, but he's a modest contender on our figures even with a first-time visor to try.

runners_data.name: Animato
runners_data.note: Fitted with a tongue-tie and most recently seen running 6th and 5th in shorter contests, this true hold-up type has been squeezed into a midfield slot on the pace map because the rear is already occupied — the honest read is that she arrives without a win or a place in this going category across seven runs, which is the more telling concern.
runners_data.comment: Held comfortably in a Hamilton handicap last time on a trip that didn't suit, this gelding wants further and has at least dropped a long way in the weights. He's proven at today's trip and ground, but he's the bottom-rated runner here and remains without a win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Arctic Fox
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up performer who has placed three times on good ground from 10 runs in similar conditions but has never won in those situations; trainer Todhunter has hit at 1/3 over the past fortnight, and Arctic Fox's two recent placed efforts over 14-16f suggest she retains ability, but age and that winless record in this going profile are limiting factors.
runners_data.comment: Typically a picture of consistency racing off a fair mark, this mare looks overdue an upturn after a well-beaten run for no obvious reason here last time. She's proven at today's trip, handles cut in the ground, and ranks fourth of six on our figures, making her one to note on a return to form.

races.paceDynamic: Laravie is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no rival likely to seriously contest her for the lead over this 2m1f trip on good ground at Carlisle, she is set to dictate at a comfortable, sustainable tempo from the outset. Tarbat Ness will press into a prominent position behind her, but with Rupert The Prince also a natural prominent type, there will be a quiet tussle for the places just off the pace — though Rupert The Prince is unlikely to secure that position as comfortably as their instincts would demand, having been pushed back by the volume of prominent types in this small field. The hold-up horses — Cascade Hall, Animato, and Arctic Fox — will track in the rear, with Animato's redistribution from their natural hold-up role meaning the closing sector may not be as strongly contested from behind as it first appears. This race shape strongly favours Laravie's profile if she can control the tempo, but the 2m1f distance on a flat, fair track gives hold-up closers like Cascade Hall — a genuine H-type with good good-ground form — the best chance of running her down if the pace is truly modest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Laravie Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Laravie bowls along at a comfortable gallop and faces no serious pace pressure through the middle stages.
scenarios.body: Laravie sets an uncontested tempo over 2m1f, conserving enough energy to hold on as closers make their runs, with Joanna Mason likely to judge the pace expertly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If Laravie's pace is genuinely slow and the hold-up horses produce a strong finishing surge in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Cascade Hall is the best credentialled genuine closer in the field with multiple good-ground wins and a strong recent record at this sort of distance, making her the chief beneficiary if the front-runner is collared.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out
scenarios.trigger: If Tarbat Ness challenges Laravie more assertively than expected and the race develops into a sustained battle between the two.
scenarios.body: A contested pace from mid-race suits neither hold-up runner and burns off Laravie faster than her lone-leader script requires, opening the door for Tarbat Ness to assert in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles Positions
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is erratic or there is significant interference that scrambles the field's running positions in the early stages.
scenarios.body: Rupert The Prince, a natural prominent type forced out of role, could benefit if a messy race allows them to find a more forward position than the pace map suggests, though their recent form over this trip is modest.

watchPoints.text: Laravie has won four of her last five and dictates pace here — if Joanna Mason gets a clear, uncontested lead from the off, she will be very hard to peg back over 2m1f.
Cascade Hall is the most dangerous closer in the race but needs the pace to be genuinely modest — watch whether Laravie's early splits give the hold-up horses a realistic chance of closing.
Rupert The Prince's natural desire to race prominently may lead to early position-jostling with Tarbat Ness, potentially unsettling both runners' rhythm in the first half-mile.

Animato was last seen racing just 9 days ago — watch the market move for any signal that Donald McCain is happy to run them back so quickly, as this quick return could be a positive or negative depending on the horse's well-being.

Arctic Fox is a 10-year-old, and while the flat Carlisle track suits hold-up types in theory, monitor whether the jockey (Josephine Gordon) elects to ride closer to the pace than the horse's historical style suggests given the moderate pace likely to be set.

races.name: Caledonia Park Designer Dash Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Another Investment
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type trained by Nigel Tinkler whose recent form string shows a worrying sequence of poor finishes (00-002), and the ⚠ fade flag reinforces concerns about finishing effort even on a suitable going; 14 days since last run is fine but the pattern is hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Showed a clear step forward when second at Doncaster last time, beaten a length and a quarter off a marginally lower mark after five winless starts. Our top-rated runner on 85, well suited by today's trip and going, and the one to beat despite sitting below the level of his last success.

runners_data.name: Thistle Nil
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old arrives on the back of a six-furlong win on Soft at her last start, but drops back to Good ground here where her record from similar conditions is unproven across only one run; genuine hold-up runner who needs the pace to truly collapse in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: A head-verdict maiden success at Ayr last time marked a big leap forward from an educational debut, coming over today's trip on soft ground. That level of form has yet to be confirmed, though, and our figures leave him at the foot of this field on 62.

runners_data.name: No Return
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old has the most consistent recent form of the closers, placing twice at 6f on Good ground in the last five runs, and suits this trip well; a natural hold-up horse who will need the pace to be more honest than expected to pounce from her rearward position.
runners_data.comment: Continued a run of steady efforts when beaten two lengths off a 2lb higher mark at Hamilton last time, though still winless in his last six starts. Racing off a fair weight and proven over today's trip, he's second on our figures at 79 and the main threat, but needs more to get his head in front.

runners_data.name: Lumenbourg
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner here for Julie Camacho, fitted with a visor, and capable of controlling this from flag to finish in a small field with no rivals willing to take her on early; her Good-ground record (8/15 similar-going runs placed or better) suggests she handles the surface, though her STYLE_FIT tag is a minor flag if the race somehow gets away from her.
runners_data.comment: A fair reflection of current form when fourth, beaten two and a quarter lengths off the same mark last time, with a win among his last five starts. Suited by today's trip and going and sporting a first-time visor, he sits only mid-pack on our figures at 70 despite the recent upturn.

runners_data.name: Invincible Ruby
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's four-year-old has genuine ability at this trip on Good ground — including a win — but holds a natural hold-up style that the overcrowded rear has pushed onto the map into midfield; the redistribution context matters because she is unlikely to be prominent despite how she appears, meaning she needs a stronger gallop than this race is likely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Third beaten two lengths off an identical mark last time, a fair effort in keeping with her level, with a win in her last six starts. Effective over today's trip on quick ground, she sits third in our figures on 78 and rates a leading threat, though she'll need more than a repeat effort to prevail.

runners_data.name: Sherlock
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's four-year-old wears blinkers and ran just nine days ago, bringing freshness and a natural prominent style that makes her the most logical pace companion to Lumenbourg; her form on Good ground at 6f is solid (two runner-up finishes in the last five), and proximity to the leader is her chief asset in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Racked up a pair of runner-up efforts among his last six starts, the latest coming at Hamilton when second, beaten two and a quarter lengths off an unchanged mark. First-time blinkers and a quick nine-day turnaround add interest, and he rates a leading danger on our figures at 70, even without a win to his name and with the yard out of sorts of late.

runners_data.name: Fan Mail
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old wears a hood (p) and has been placed at 6f on Good and Soft, but her natural style is a genuine hold-up game that the field's congestion at the rear has pushed forward on the map — in reality she will be chasing from behind in what is unlikely to be a fast enough pace to favour her.
runners_data.comment: Consistently below his best of late, without a win in his last six starts, and used up too soon when beaten five and a half lengths in a handicap at Ripon last time. First-time cheekpieces may help sharpen him up over his favoured trip, but he needs a definite improvement and sits only seventh on our figures at 66.

runners_data.name: Too Much
runners_data.note: David Thompson's six-year-old showed some form at 5f on Good and 8f on Soft, which hints at versatility but also inconsistency; a true hold-up runner whose trainer has had no winners in the last 14 days from seven runners, and the 26-day break combined with a modest recent record makes this a speculative entry in an unfavourable race shape.
runners_data.comment: Failed to fire on soft ground when beaten five lengths in a handicap at this course last time, continuing a spell out of sorts without a win in her last five starts. She does have course form and acts well on quicker ground, which today's surface may suit better, leaving her a workable sixth on our figures at 69.

runners_data.name: Maui Breeze
runners_data.note: Wilf Storey's four-year-old wears a hood and has been tackling longer trips (7f-10f) in recent starts with limited success; the drop back to 6f is a positive but her hold-up style is the real constraint — pushed onto the map away from the rear purely because of field congestion, she will likely race deeper than shown and finds this an unlikely pace scenario to suit.
runners_data.comment: Struggling to find any consistency, without a win in her last six starts, she matched her recent level when beaten five lengths in a handicap at Pontefract last time. First-time cheekpieces offer some hope of sharpening her up over a trip and surface that suit, but she remains below the level she showed earlier this year and is only eighth on our figures at 64.

races.paceDynamic: Lumenbourg is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 6f handicap at Carlisle on Good turf, and with no genuine rivals pressing for the lead, she is set to dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo from the outset. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Invincible Ruby, Fan Mail, Too Much, and Maui Breeze are all natural closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the rear is overcrowded, not because they will genuinely race prominently. Sherlock is the one other horse capable of tracking Lumenbourg from a prominent position, and with the pace light and the gallop not pressured, the tempo is unlikely to be strong enough to set up a dramatic late-finishing burst from the genuine hold-up brigade. This race shape firmly favours horses who can track the pace from a prominent or close-up position and use that proximity when the field straightens for home, rather than those forced wide or deep from the rear in what will likely be a moderate tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lumenbourg Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lumenbourg leads at a comfortable gallop and Sherlock tracks without applying pressure, the front two dominate the finish.
scenarios.body: Lumenbourg sets an uncontested pace and, with no one willing to commit early, the advantage built through the middle portions of the race proves too great to reel in from behind; Sherlock, tracking throughout, has the cleanest path to any challenger.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Emerge Late From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough through the first three furlongs to drain Lumenbourg's stamina before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: In this less likely shape, the genuine hold-up horses — particularly Invincible Ruby and No Return — arrive with late momentum, but note that several of them are natural closers squeezed into midfield rather than their true position, tempering confidence in a clean run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Sherlock moves up to genuinely press Lumenbourg through the middle stages and turns the race into a two-horse battle from three furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A contested lead drains both principals earlier than ideal and opens a slim door for horses like No Return, who has consistent 6f form on Good ground; Sherlock's blinkers and recent 9-day freshness could see her carry the fight to the line if Lumenbourg weakens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If horses drawn wide struggle to find economical positions and the race becomes muddled with multiple moves at once around the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: In this chaotic scenario, race position is scrambled and hold-up horses caught wide burn energy they cannot afford; Thistle Nil's recent winning form and Invincible Ruby's proven Good-ground record give them the best residual claims if the shape dissolves.

watchPoints.text: Lumenbourg's ability to coast through unchallenged in the first two furlongs is the pivotal factor — if she crosses cleanly from her draw and settles in front without being pressured, the race is likely hers to lose.

Sherlock is the one horse whose prominent style gives her a genuine chance of tracking Lumenbourg honestly; watch whether she commits early enough from her draw to secure that second position, as falling back into the pack would leave the front-runner unopposed and harder to catch.

Invincible Ruby has won twice at 6f on Good ground and is the most dangerous closer in the race, but her redistribution from a true hold-up position means she needs an unusually honest pace to deliver — monitor how the opening splits compare to standard 6f Good ground times at Carlisle.

No Return has shown consistent placed form at 6f on Good going for Charlie Johnston and represents the hold-up brigade's steadiest option if the gallop is stronger than expected; her proximity in the final two furlongs will signal whether the pace has been truly sustainable.

Fan Mail's hood and the sheer number of hold-up types in this field means the final furlong could see a cluster of closers arriving simultaneously — watch for interference or crowding in the last 100 yards if Lumenbourg's lead narrows.
